{"id":"MM-458","title":"Phase 3: Any-PDS rescue and migration destination — capability-gated finalize","description":"Part of <issue id="d5cb6e3d-f781-4ecb-aebf-c954915b3708" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-452/obsign-without-custos-first-class-any-pds-wallet-support-epic">MM-452</issue>. Design: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md` §Phase 3.

## Why

Recovering an account is the worst possible moment to present a hosting decision with only one viable answer. Today every leg of sovereign disaster recovery (`disaster_recovery.rs`) and outbound migration works against any PDS — offline service-auth JWT verified via [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>), standard `createAccount`/`importRepo`/`uploadBlob`/`activateAccount` — **except** the finalize: `finalize_migration_core` unconditionally mints the destination sovereign session via `/v1/sessions/sovereign`, which only Custos serves. A reference-PDS destination would die at the last step, after the identity op already landed.

## What

Branch the injected `ensure_session` step on the destination's `sovereignSessions` capability (<issue id="e2abaa52-2747-4daf-8c10-209294bd5183" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-454/phase-0b-custos-capability-extension-in-describeserver-self">MM-454</issue>):

* **Capability present (Custos):** today's behavior — mint + persist the sovereign session before deactivating the source.
* **Capability absent:** durably persist the Bearer session already held from the migration `createAccount` (via the existing `OAuthClient::new_bearer` + versioned `{did}:oauth-tokens` record) as the destination credential, preserving the strict activate → durable-credential → deactivate ordering. Post-cutover session lifecycle then rides Phase 2's password unlock path (<issue id="7d621f07-95f0-490d-a547-4f75b3e9f24c" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-457/phase-2-foreign-pds-session-provider-password-createsession-unlock">MM-457</issue>).

Same branch serves both flows for free: sovereign disaster recovery to a non-Custos destination, and normal outbound migration between two non-Custos hosts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Disaster recovery rebuilds an account onto a reference PDS end-to-end from the iCloud backups, with the same abort-safety ordering (a credential-persistence failure leaves nothing half-live and is retryable).
2. Outbound migration to a non-Custos destination finalizes without ever calling `/v1/sessions/sovereign`.
3. Custos-destination behavior is byte-identical to today (existing orchestrator tests unchanged).
4. The destination-picker UI presents Custos and other-PDS destinations with equal weight — the Custos pitch is its capabilities, not the only working button.

content.text:
Done — [PR #453](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/453), MM-458 moved to In Review with the PR attached.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The fix was mostly a rename.** `ensure_didweb_session_persisted` already did precisely what a non-Custos did:plc destination needs — validate the `createAccount` Bearer pair's `sub`/`aud` and write it into `{did}:oauth-tokens`. The did:web case and the foreign-host case are the same underlying fact ("nothing here can mint a sovereign session"), reached by different routes. Recognizing that turned a new subsystem into `ensure_bearer_session_persisted` plus a four-line decision function.
- **The `reached: false` question is the interesting design call.** This codebase has an established asymmetry (`share_recovery::host_offers_escrow`, the create gate): treat "couldn't ask" as "not offered" only when the wrong guess degrades safely. Here I kept sovereign on unreached, because step 1 of the cutover (`activateAccount`) has already succeeded against that host — so an unreached probe is a describeServer blink, and inferring absence from it would quietly downgrade a Custos destination's credential. That also happens to be what makes AC3 ("byte-identical") literally true.
- **Both destination pickers already passed AC4** — bare URL fields, no Custos button. The real gap wasn't equal weight, it was that the user was never told what actually differs between destinations. That's why the UI addition is a factual sign-in readout gated on `reached`, not a marketing panel.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Two environment notes: the sandbox blocks socket binds, so both the vite harness and the `httpmock`-based Rust tests need `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` (you can adjust this with `/sandbox`). The full suite is green at 664 passed / 0 failed with it off.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/pr-review-comments

# Batch PR Review-Comment Triage

Pull every unresolved review thread on the current PR in one command, then triage the batch. The user should never have to paste review comments one at a time.

## Fetch unresolved threads

Determine the PR number for the current branch (`gh pr view --json number -q .number`), then:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){
  repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){
    pullRequest(number:$pr){
      reviewThreads(first:100){
        nodes{
          isResolved isOutdated path line
          comments(first:30){nodes{author{login} body url}}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}' -F owner=<owner> -F repo=<repo> -F pr=<number> \
| jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]
       | select(.isResolved==false)
       | {path, line, isOutdated,
          comments: [.comments.nodes[] | {author: .author.login, url, body}]}]'
```

Also fetch top-level (non-thread) review bodies and issue comments if the bot posts summaries there:

```bash
gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments
```

## Triage the batch

For each unresolved thread, classify before fixing anything:

1. **Correctness / security / portability** — verify the claim against the actual code, then fix if real. Automated reviewers assert confidently and are sometimes wrong; refute with evidence when they are.
2. **Legitimate but out of scope** — file a follow-up issue rather than growing the PR.
3. **Pure style nit / preference** — decline with a one-line reason.

Present the full disposition table (thread → classification → action) to the user in ONE message before applying fixes, so they approve the batch rather than each item. Note that every fix-commit re-triggers CI and (for assertive bots like CodeRabbit) a fresh review round that tends to find one more micro-nit — batch fixes into a single commit where possible.

## Resolving threads

After pushing fixes, reply/resolve via:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='mutation($id:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$id}){thread{isResolved}}}' -F id=<threadId>
```

(Include `id` in the reviewThreads query above if you plan to resolve threads programmatically.)

lines: - `src/recovery.rs` — Recovery override module: `build_recovery_override(pds_client, did, unauthorized_op_cid) -> Result<SignedRecoveryOp, RecoveryError>` (fetches audit log, identifies fork point, builds counter-operation restoring pre-unauthorized state, signs with per-DID device key), `submit_recovery_override(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, RecoveryError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, updates cached log and DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_recovery_override_cmd`, `submit_recovery_override_cmd`. Types: `SignedRecoveryOp` { diff, signed_op }, `RecoveryState` { did, signed_op }, `RecoveryError` (RECOVERY_WINDOW_EXPIRED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED_CHANGE_NOT_FOUND)

- `src/identity_removal.rs` — Permanent identity removal (5 Tauri IPC commands): `request_identity_removal(did)` (gets a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` — a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SessionRequired` so the UI runs `unlockIdentity` first — then calls `com.atproto.server.requestAccountDelete`, which emails a single-use code), `confirm_identity_removal(did, password, token)` (calls `deleteAccount` FIRST — a bad password/code is `InvalidToken` with nothing mutated — then persists a durable pending-removal marker and runs `retire_and_wipe`), `tombstone_identity(did)` (resume path: retire + wipe only, for when `confirm` deleted the account but the tombstone/wipe failed and the single-use code is already spent; for a did:web there is no tombstone to retry, so the resume is the local wipe alone), and `list_pending_removals()` (the launch-reconciliation source: the DIDs whose post-delete tombstone/wipe never finished), and `forget_identity_locally(did)` (the local-only escape hatch: wipes the DID's Keychain material and clears any pending marker with NO network step, returning `wasLastIdentity`. For an identity whose PDS account no longer exists — deleted from another device, purged server-side, or migrated away — `deleteAccount` can only answer with an opaque 401 indistinguishable from a wrong password (the PDS is not an account-existence oracle, see `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs`), so the request/confirm flow can never make progress. It deliberately does NOT tombstone the did:plc — the DID may already be retired or now live on another PDS — so it only promises to remove the identity from THIS device; biometric-gated in the frontend). Shared core `retire_and_wipe` is **method-aware** and owns the branch both commands go through: a **did:plc** runs `tombstone_and_wipe` (fetch the audit-log head as `prev`, build+sign a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure`, self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN call `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry; the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested), while a **did:web** skips the tombstone leg entirely and goes straight to the wipe, never contacting plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`. A did:web has no PLC log, so routing it through the tombstone path would 404 on the audit-log fetch and wedge the flow permanently: the account gone and its single-use email code spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary precisely because `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same code; guarding only the entry point would leave the wedge reachable. Retiring a did:web network-wide means removing its `did.json` from the domain — an operator action outside the wallet's control, which the UI states rather than simulating. **Post-delete recovery marker:** the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds, `confirm_identity_removal` records the DID in the durable `pending-removals` Keychain index (a JSON array), *before* the tombstone's network round trip — the step iOS is most likely to interrupt by suspending the app. Both `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` clear the marker (best-effort) once `retire_and_wipe` completes — including on the did:web path, which is what keeps an interrupted did:web removal from becoming permanent retry state. On launch the UI calls `list_pending_removals()` and, for any listed DID, resumes straight to the idempotent retry rather than the request flow — which would fail against the already-deleted account. No PDS/DB changes: both `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints already exist and are method-agnostic, and the did:plc tombstone is the DID-level network messaging the PDS can't do (it holds no rotation key, ADR-0001). Types: `RemovalOutcome` { tombstoneCid (null when the removed DID has no tombstone leg — a did:web), wasLastIdentity }, `RemovalError` (SESSION_REQUIRED, REQUEST_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_TOKEN, ACCOUNT_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, TOMBSTONE_SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, LOCAL_WIPE_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, NETWORK_ERROR)

- `src/migrate.rs` — Self-signed account-migration identity leg (ADR-0002 path 1): builds and locally device-key-signs the DID-repointing PLC op and submits it directly to plc.directory — no email token, no `signPlcOperation` round-trip. `build_migration_op(pds_client, dest_client, did) -> Result<SignedMigrationOp, MigrateError>` (fetches audit log for `prev` + current state, reads `getRecommendedDidCredentials` from the DESTINATION PDS via the passed-in authed `OAuthClient`, assembles the op with the device key preserved at `rotationKeys[0]`, runs the strict pre-sign guard, signs with the per-DID device key), `submit_migration_op(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, MigrateError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, refreshes cached log + DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_migration_op_cmd`, `submit_migration_op_cmd`. Pure helpers: `guard_migration_op` (strict allowlist), `recommended_verification_methods`/`recommended_services` (RecommendedCredentials JSON → typed maps), `latest_op_state` (current state from newest non-nullified audit entry), `build_migration_diff`. Types: `SignedMigrationOp` { diff, signed_op }, `MigrationState` { did, dest_oauth_client, signed_op }, `MigrationInputs`; `MigrateError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_RECOMMENDED_CREDENTIALS, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MIGRATION_NOT_READY). The destination-PDS OAuth login is NOT owned here — the migration orchestrator authenticates and populates `MigrationState.dest_oauth_client` before `build_migration_op_cmd` runs

-- `src/migration_orchestrator.rs` — wallet-authorized outbound migration state machine (ADR-0002 path 1). Fine-grained per-step Tauri commands driving the source→dest transfer: `prepare_migration` (resolve dest describeServer + source; returns `PreparedMigration { handle, sourcePdsUrl }` for the source-auth screen), `authenticate_migration_source` (password `createSession` → full-session Bearer client, mirrors `claim::authenticate_source_pds`; per ADR-0021 a full session is required to mint the source's `createAccount` service-auth token — HTTPS + account-match guards + email-2FA, password used once and never stored), `create_destination_account` (reserveSigningKey → getServiceAuth → deactivated `createAccount` → Bearer session; tolerates `DidAlreadyExists` for resume), `transfer_repo` (getRepo → importRepo; on a source `getRepo` failure it falls back to the local iCloud repo mirror `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car` when that mirror holds a CID/commit-valid snapshot for the DID, else surfaces the original source failure unchanged — the repo twin of the blob drain's mirror fallback), `transfer_blobs` (cursor-paginated `listMissingBlobs` drain), `transfer_preferences` (get→put), `verify_import` (`checkAccountStatus` completeness gate; returns `AccountStatus`), `arm_identity_leg` (populate `migrate::MigrationState.dest_oauth_client`, then run `migrate::build_migration_op_cmd`/`submit_migration_op_cmd`), `finalize_migration` (the safe cutover — **activate dest → durably persist the destination session → deactivate source → Finalized**; the source stays active until the durable credential is stored, so a crash or retry never strands the account credential-less). **Which credential gets persisted is capability-gated, not assumed**: `destination_credential` (pure, unit-tested) answers `Sovereign` or `Bearer` from the DID method plus the destination's advertised `sovereignSessions` (`pds_capabilities`, warm from `prepare_migration`'s describeServer). A host that **answered** and does not advertise it — the reference PDS, bsky.social, any spec-compliant PDS, or a Custos running with the capability off — takes the Bearer branch, since minting against a route it does not serve would fail *after* the identity op already landed. A did:web takes it unconditionally (no rotation keys to sign the proof). A host that could **not be asked** keeps the sovereign branch: `activateAccount` has already succeeded against it by then, so `reached: false` is a describeServer blink, not grounds to downgrade a Custos destination's credential. The same branch serves outbound migration and sovereign disaster recovery, which share this command. Pure cores split out for testability (`ensure_phase_did` gate, `create_destination_account_impl`, `drain_missing_blobs`, `transfer_repo_impl`, `transfer_preferences_impl`, `import_reconciles`, `activate_destination_account`/`deactivate_source_account` cutover halves, `destination_credential`, `ensure_sovereign_session_persisted` (idempotent skip when a persisted record's refresh token is still unexpired, else `sovereign_session::sovereign_login_impl` → persist), `ensure_bearer_session_persisted` (the same idempotent skip, then sub/aud-validate and persist the pair `createAccount` already issued into the same `{did}:oauth-tokens` record — from that write on `session_provider` restores and refreshes it identically, and re-unlock rides `password_unlock`'s password `createSession` route), and the `*_core` mutex-parameterized command cores; `finalize_migration_core` takes an injected `ensure_session` step so its activate → session → deactivate ordering is unit-testable without a Keychain or live PDS). `MigrationError` (MIGRATION_NOT_READY, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE, SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED, TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH, INSECURE_SOURCE_URL, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR, SERVICE_AUTH_FAILED, ACCOUNT_CREATION_FAILED, DESTINATION_CONFLICT, REPO_TRANSFER_FAILED, BLOB_TRANSFER_FAILED, PREFERENCES_TRANSFER_FAILED, VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE, ACTIVATION_FAILED, SOVEREIGN_LOGIN_FAILED, SESSION_PERSIST_FAILED, DEACTIVATION_FAILED, NETWORK_ERROR — SOVEREIGN_LOGIN_FAILED and SESSION_PERSIST_FAILED are the retryable cutover-mint failures that leave the source active, aborting before deactivation). Migration state is in-memory only (`AppState.orchestration_state`); an app kill restarts from `prepare_migration`, but the destination session it persists (via `identity_store` `{did}:oauth-tokens`) survives — a restarted wallet reconstructs the destination client from that record (`sovereign_session::stored_bearer_client`), not from `OutboundMigrationState`.
